## 固定收益開篇主論點

美國與伊朗再度交戰，帶動油價大幅上漲、通膨補償升高，也強化聯準會可能於本月升息的預期，美國公債因而在9月1日延續跌勢。2年期殖利率上升5.8個基點至4.401%，5年期上升5.5個基點至4.556%，10年期上升4.8個基點至4.799%，30年期則上升3.2個基點至5.275%。

賣壓主要集中在前端至10年期區段，使殖利率曲線溫和呈現熊市趨平。2年期與10年期利差收窄1個基點至39.8個基點，2年期與30年期利差收窄2.6個基點至87.4個基點。過去一週，兩段曲線分別趨平5.7與11.7個基點，反映投資人上調預期政策利率路徑的速度快於長期殖利率。

本次10年期名目殖利率升幅主要來自通膨補償。10年期損益兩平通膨率上升3.7個基點至2.358%，10年期實質殖利率上升1.1個基點至2.441%；前一個交易日的殖利率升幅則幾乎全由實質殖利率推動。美國再度空襲伊朗、德黑蘭還擊，且兩艘試圖駛離荷莫茲海峽的油輪遭投射物擊中後，WTI大漲5.83%至$90.76，布蘭特原油上漲5.23%至$95.22。

主席Kevin Warsh在傑克森霍爾的訊息已使市場為更緊縮的政策預作準備，此時能源衝擊進一步升高升息機率。利率期貨顯示，9月15日至16日會議至少升息25個基點的機率為66.2%，高於一週前的39.6%。聯準會理事Michael Barr則從決策委員會中間立場提出新的條件式訊號：若後續數據顯示通膨正朝2%回落，官員可以保持耐心；若通膨降溫不足，則應果斷行動。

美國製造業數據並未提供明確答案。供應管理協會指數由7月的55.6降至8月的54.6，低於55.2的市場共識，新訂單也轉弱；但支付價格指數仍高達71.1，供應商交貨時間進一步拉長。7月職缺則略增，顯示勞動需求低迷但穩定，並未崩落。這組數據讓聯準會看見工業動能放緩，卻沒有出現足以明確支持再次按兵不動的成本降溫。

殖利率上升衝擊風險資產，但未造成全面市場失序。標普500指數下跌0.71%，那斯達克100指數下跌1.29%，半導體指數下跌2.14%；美元指數上升0.24%，黃金期貨下跌1.21%。VIX升至16.34，仍遠低於急性市場壓力常見的水準。美國投資級債利差小幅擴大，高收益債利差擴幅較為明顯，硬通貨新興市場債利差也小幅走闊。

因此，本交易日的核心並非資金因避險而湧入公債，而是全球重新評估承擔存續期風險的代價。油價提高近期通膨門檻，市場上調央行利率預期，政府與企業供給則持續爭奪資金。日本10年期公債殖利率觸及3%後，標售仍獲得尚可需求；英國長期公債殖利率升至1998年以來未見水準；歐元區通膨也強化ECB升息理由。融資市場仍然開放，沙烏地阿拉伯發行$32.5億伊斯蘭債券時獲得逾$150億訂單；但發行市場展現韌性，仍未阻止信用較弱的主權與企業債遭到大幅重新定價。

## 油價、製造業與Barr讓聯準會9月升息仍有可能

本輪油價走勢反映荷莫茲海峽周邊再度出現實體安全威脅，而不只是言辭轉變。美國指控德黑蘭企圖在海峽布雷並攻擊位於約旦的美軍基地，隨後對伊朗目標發動空襲。伊朗表示已採取報復行動，阿曼外海兩艘超級油輪也遭投射物擊中。在此之前，局勢曾相對平靜數週；華府當時著重經濟施壓，而臨時和平協議破裂後，雙方都未展現太大意願重啟談判。

WTI收在$90以上、布蘭特原油升破$95，使能源重新成為通膨討論的直接傳導管道。10年期損益兩平通膨率上升3.7個基點，顯示投資人並未將衝擊只視為短暫的地緣政治新聞；不過，其2.358%的水準仍不代表長期通膨預期已經失去錨定。實質殖利率同步上升，則顯示政策、供給及財政不確定性仍高，投資人也要求更高的通膨調整後補償。

市場對聯準會的預期已大幅轉變，但尚未形成定論。期貨顯示，聯準會在目前3.50%至3.75%的目標區間上於9月升息的機率約為三分之二，明顯高於一週前的39.6%，但委員會選擇等待的可能性仍不可忽視。市場正在判斷，官員會直接回應能源的第一輪衝擊，還是要等到有證據顯示衝擊已擴散至更廣泛的價格與預期後才行動。

Barr的談話明確呈現這項條件。他表示，若數據足以讓官員相信通膨正朝2%降溫，便可花更多時間觀察；若降溫程度不足，央行就應果斷升息。Reuters將Barr描述為立場相對中間的決策官員，因此這項表態格外值得注意。7月會議已有3名官員主張升息並提出異議，分別是明尼亞波利斯聯準銀行總裁Neel Kashkari、克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack及達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Lorie Logan。

後續通膨報告仍是檢驗Barr所提條件的關鍵，但最新活動數據並未呈現需求轉弱、成本同時下降的良性組合，官員因而不容易安心等待。ISM製造業PMI下降1點至54.6，雖仍處於擴張區間，卻低於55.2的預測中位數與另一項55.0的預測。新訂單由56.7較大幅降至53.7，顯示製造業內部需求放緩。

成本與供應指標則朝不同方向發展。支付價格維持在71.1，供應商交貨指數由58.9升至59.3；該指數上升代表交貨速度更慢。受訪企業表示，鋁、鋼、銅、電氣產品、燃料、記憶體產品及半導體價格均上漲，部分金屬與電子產品也出現短缺。ISM的Susan Spence指出，58%的受訪者評論偏負面，企業提到價格波動、交期延長、伊朗衝突與關稅等問題。

其他近期指標顯示經濟放緩而非收縮。物流經理人指數由7月的68.9降至8月的66.6，但仍在擴張區間。截至8月29日當週，Redbook同店銷售年增率由9.1%加快至9.6%，家庭支出的名目訊號仍強。7月職缺由718萬增至727萬，略低於731萬的預測中位數，離職與解僱人數則下降。這些數據都不足以推翻較疲弱的ISM總指數，但合在一起也看不出需求突然斷裂。

這項組合解釋了為何製造業動能減弱之際，美債前端仍然遭到拋售。產出指標走弱通常會降低維持緊縮的必要性，但支付價格及廣泛的投入成本壓力使通膨風險持續存在。市場的反應已不只取決於整體成長，也愈來愈重視能源、關稅，以及AI帶動的設備與電力需求是否妨礙成本壓力降溫。

長端另有一項考驗。30年期殖利率回升至5.275%，約與財政部長Scott Bessent在8月19日宣布擴大買回前的水準相同。相關買回預定9月9日才開始，財政部目前只表示，10年至30年期證券的操作規模至少會加倍。這項宣布一度改善市場氣氛，卻沒有消除政府本身的融資需求，也未排除企業借款人對資金的競爭。

8月供給創紀錄後，市場預期9月投資級企業債發行量將達約$2,150億，其中很大一部分與AI建設有關。今年30年期殖利率已有55個交易日收在5%以上，為2006年以來任一年度最多；進入9月時，該殖利率也已較2026年低點上升約65個基點。選擇權交易員已付費防範殖利率進一步上升，其中包括一筆成本$650萬、押注30年期殖利率可在11月底前升至5.7%的部位。

最新曲線走勢並不像長端失控崩跌。較短期指標殖利率的升幅大於30年期，美債市場波動也維持受控。現券交易量較前一交易日異常高的水準回落：FINRA記錄的美債面額成交量為$1.262兆，比8月31日少30.6%，其中附息名目公債為$1.037兆。成交量下降不能證明投資人的交易方向，但顯示此次殖利率調整並未伴隨另一波交易量暴增。

## 政策與財政壓力升高之際，日本3%殖利率吸引需求

日本10年期公債殖利率自1996年以來首次觸及3%，之後報3.005%，較一年前約為目前一半的水準快速重新定價。漲勢遍及整條曲線：2年期殖利率升至1.81%，為31年高點；5年期觸及2.265%的歷史新高；20年期升至3.885%；30年期則接近約4.18%的歷史最高收盤水準。

緊接而來的10年期公債標售顯示，較高殖利率開始吸引需求。投標倍數由前次的2.56升至3.29，並略高於過去12個月平均的3.26；標售尾差收窄，MUFJ Morgan Stanley承接22%的發行量。標售結果使10年期殖利率在觸及3%後略為回落，與前一週疲弱的2年期標售形成對比。

需求雖然穩健，仍稱不上非常強勁。SMBC Nikko策略師Miki Den表示，投資人看來要求殖利率高於3%，而本次標售平均殖利率已足夠接近這道門檻，因此成功吸引買盤。本週四的30年期公債標售將是更嚴格的考驗，因為超長天期債券更容易受到財政擴張、增發風險及日本利率長期正常化影響。

市場對9月政策行動的定價已接近完成。Bloomberg最新報導顯示，隔夜指數交換反映BOJ在9月17日至18日會議採取行動的機率約為99%，一個月前則不到一半。央行上次於6月將政策利率升至1%，為31年最高。短期與中期殖利率上升，如今反映市場預期BOJ將再次回應通膨及日圓持續疲弱。

Bessent在北卡羅來納州舉行的20國集團會議期間與BOJ總裁植田和男會面後，進一步強化這項預期。美國財政部表示，Bessent強力支持日本採取果斷的市場與貨幣措施，以處理日圓遭顯著低估的問題；他並指出匯率疲弱正加劇日本國內通膨，也強調政策溝通應穩定預期、避免匯率過度波動。

不過，華府究竟多直接地討論日本貨幣政策，雙方說法出現分歧。美國財政部次長Erin Browne表示，Bessent曾告訴植田和男與日本財務大臣片山皋月，日本的下一步應是升息。片山皋月否認與他討論貨幣政策的具體操作，並強調BOJ依法獨立；但她表示，雙方同意日圓有序波動對全球金融穩定十分重要，協調行動也一直有益。

這項差異並未減輕市場壓力。東京交易時段，日圓跌破160兌1美元；此前一個月，日本已進行規模創紀錄的¥15.4兆干預，美國也參與7月31日的操作。Bessent愈來愈明確地把BOJ緊縮視為優於反覆干預匯市的選項，而美國財政部的正式會談紀要，也將美方對日圓的疑慮與日本國內通膨問題連結起來。

財政政策同樣加劇JGB殖利率的上行壓力。日本各省廳針對2027財政年度提出約¥143兆預算申請，總額創歷史新高，也超過本年度初始預算與前一年度追加預算合計約¥140.6兆的規模。經濟產業省申請金額超過前一年度的5倍，國防與社會福利申請也雙雙創紀錄。

部分增幅來自首相高市早苗的規畫：把傳統上透過追加預算編列的支出移入初始預算，並為成長投資建立多年期架構。這能提高透明度，卻不會消除融資需求。部分支出金額尚未確定，可能在預算程序中進一步增加；財務省也已為償債支出申請創紀錄的¥36.6兆。

高市早苗表示，希望把新債發行控制在¥40兆以下。能否達成，將取決於政府多大幅度刪減各省廳申請，以及實際收入能否符合假設。日本政府總債務仍高於GDP的200%，政府估算2026財政年度償債成本時採用的長期利率假設為3%；如今，指標10年期公債的市場殖利率已觸及這一水準。

殖利率上升也形成反向的需求管道。10年期公債殖利率已高於銀行的融資成本與壽險公司的負債成本，日本國內債券相對海外證券對本地機構更具競爭力。另一方面，國際投資人目前占每月JGB現券交易約三分之二，遠高於2009年的12%，使市場除了受國內機構資產負債表需求影響，也更容易受到全球部位調整左右。

本次標售證明3%可以吸引資金，卻未建立殖利率上限。BOJ可能升息、日圓疲弱及創紀錄的預算申請，都指向更高利率的環境；與此同時，殖利率本身上升也改善國內投資人持有JGB的經濟效益。週四30年期標售將顯示，這股需求能否延伸至最容易受到未來供給與償債風險影響的曲線區段。

## 歐洲通膨與英國利率延續全球緊縮循環

歐元區通膨率由7月的2.9%加快至8月的3.3%，創2023年9月以來最高，並符合預測中位數。市場因此幾乎確定ECB將在9月10日把存款利率調升25個基點至2.50%，這將是ECB在2026年的第二次升息。

通膨組成卻不像總指數那樣全面偏鷹。核心通膨由2.5%降至2.4%，服務通膨由3.3%放緩至3.0%。油氣價格高漲推升德國、法國、義大利與西班牙的總體通膨，但基礎指標下降，顯示廣泛的第二輪效應尚未明顯浮現。

德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel認為核心與服務通膨下降是正面發展，並表示下一次政策決定相對容易預測，與市場已完全反映9月升息一致。立陶宛央行總裁Gediminas Simkus對下週以後的政策路徑看法更為強硬。他認為9月升息並不足夠，理由包括天然氣及農產品價格上漲，以及歐洲成長強於預期，這些因素都應使預測利率路徑上移。

相較於9月決策本身，這兩種立場更清楚界定了下一階段的爭論。現行存款利率為2.25%，低於ECB首席經濟學家Philip Lane所稱中性區間上緣的2.5%；升息25個基點便會觸及該界線。市場定價顯示未來一年還會升息兩次，但經濟學家與部分決策官員認為ECB很可能在9月後停止升息。12月官員取得新一輪工作人員預測時，可能成為重新評估的時點。

英國公債在假期後補跌，是本輪全球債市賣壓最嚴重的市場之一。10年期殖利率一度上升11個基點至5.25%，30年期升至5.89%，為1998年5月以來最高。市場反映英國央行至明年2月前將升息兩次，既因能源衝擊，也因英國財政空間有限，可能使長天期公債承受格外大的壓力。

英國央行決策委員Catherine Mann進一步強化國內維持緊縮的理由。她表示，經濟成長較上次會議時增強，勞動市場似乎正在穩定，通膨則略高於預期。Mann在前次會議投票支持升息25個基點，並主張即使利率略微設得過高，日後仍可修正，顯示她認為放任通膨風險持續的代價更大。

市場已完全反映英國央行年底前會升息，但9月採取行動的機率僅約15%。近期房市與信用數據可以解釋部分謹慎態度。7月房貸核准件數由58,215件降至56,053件，低於59,400件的預期，並創2024年1月以來最低。伊朗衝突前平均2年期固定房貸利率為4.83%，其後升至5.59%；房貸核准件數也已連續三個月低於60,000件。

房價訊號則好壞參半。Nationwide表示，8月平均房價上升0.2%至£275,465，略高於0.1%的預測，並扭轉7月下修後的0.1%跌幅。房價較一年前上升1.6%，但先前已連續三個月下跌，且仍受融資成本升高壓抑。7月無擔保消費借款由£19億增至£20億，家庭銀行存款流入則由£62億放緩至£38億，顯示消費者正透過借款及動用儲蓄，緩衝實質所得所受壓力。

以色列的政策方向相反。以色列央行降息25個基點至3.25%，為5月與7月後連續第三次降息。決策前預期勢均力敵：受訪18位經濟學家中，9位預期降息，另9位預期利率不變。其後謝克爾走弱至3.02兌1美元，但仍接近歷史強勢水準；這種強勢先前已促使出口商要求央行提供更多寬鬆支持。

央行以通膨降溫為由，並表示若排除以色列企業的海外生產，經濟活動看來較疲弱；此前因戰事收縮後，第二季GDP年化成長率仍達15.4%。政策指引仍取決於通膨、經濟活動、地緣政治及財政發展。因此，以色列降息反映其國內通膨與匯率條件，而非全球價格壓力普遍下降；若與其他已開發市場的政策路徑持續分歧，並對謝克爾形成長期壓力，這項差異本身也可能成為政策限制。

## 主權融資市場仍開放，信用結果卻明顯分歧

美國升息預期與油價上升削弱市場對較高風險債務的需求，使全球債市因存續期重新定價而出現的賣壓蔓延至新興市場。一籃子30個發展中國家主權信用違約交換已連續第4日上升。JPMorgan數據顯示，新興市場美元債利差週一已擴大6個基點至235個基點，本幣債券則延續自8月25日創紀錄高點以來的跌勢。

整體市場走弱並未關閉初級市場。沙烏地阿拉伯發行$32.5億的5年期與10年期伊斯蘭債券，訂單高峰超過$150億。10年期部分以美債殖利率加80個基點定價，較初步討論水準收窄約30個基點。資金將用於一般預算用途；交易成功顯示，即使直接承受荷莫茲衝突的經濟曝險，交易活躍且信用較強的主權借款人仍能在發行過程中改善定價。

沙烏地阿拉伯的融資需求依然龐大。石油活動減弱，使其經濟第二季出現疫情以來最嚴重的季度收縮；政府也正就至少$80億貸款進行初步協商。在本週二發債前，沙烏地阿拉伯今年已透過國內外債券募集約$60億，Saudi Aramco與公共投資基金另合計發行$110億。強勁需求降低了眼前的配售風險，卻未消除減產及區域衝突所帶來的財政影響。

塞內加爾在明確說明預定債務處理方式後，市場反應正好相反。其2028年到期歐元債券大跌6.9歐分至49.44歐分，主權利差由1,651個基點升至1,745個基點。政府與IMF就新的$22億計畫達成工作人員層級協議後，表示將依20國集團共同框架的改良版本推進債務處理。

IMF協議仍屬初步，尚待執行董事會批准，並以政府採取修正措施處理先前未揭露的債務為條件；正是這批債務曝光，導致IMF暫停先前的$18億融資安排。財政部長Cheikh Diba表示，政府偏好量身設計、干擾程度較低的重整方式，但承諾未來數週將提出執行時程與進一步細節。

債券價格下跌顯示，投資人認為這項宣布提高了債權人讓步的可能性。塞內加爾每年約需6兆西非法郎、相當於$106億的融資，今年計畫在區域市場募集約4兆西非法郎。包括總報酬交換在內的結構型融資，曾協助填補其失去國際市場融資管道後的缺口，但也受到IMF審視。新計畫最終可能降低融資成本，卻尚未確定到期債務如何處理、回收價值或執行時程。

南韓也提出另一項大型主權債供給計畫。政府擬於2027年發行222.8兆韓元債券，接近今年創紀錄的232兆韓元計畫。其中110.7兆韓元用於償還到期債務，15.9兆韓元用於支持造市操作，淨發行量約為96.3兆韓元。

這筆借款將為總統李在明的擴張政策籌資；支出預計增加12.8%至創紀錄的820.9兆韓元。南韓3年期殖利率上升6個基點至3.9%，10年期上升9個基點至4.4%。發行提案仍須國會批准，過往經驗也顯示國會可能縮減最終金額；但總額超過200兆韓元，仍令原本預期強勁半導體稅收可使發行量大幅下降的投資人失望。

巴西經濟則對本地降息形成另一種限制。第二季GDP成長0.5%，雖低於第一季的1.1%，仍高於0.4%的預測中位數；產出較一年前成長2.0%，也超過1.8%的預期。農業成長2.8%，服務業成長0.2%，工業成長0.1%；家庭消費則收縮0.4%，為三季以來首次下降。

數據組成顯示，具韌性的整體成長與對利率敏感的需求之間，差距正在擴大。營建與製造業均收縮，固定投資雖成長1.2%，速度卻遠低於第一季。8月中通膨率為4.24%，高於3%的目標，Selic利率則達14%；即使官員預期第三季經濟會再次放緩，央行加快降息循環的空間仍有限。

印度外部帳戶也更加依賴融資流量。4月至6月一季，經常帳赤字由一年前修正後的$34億、相當於GDP的0.4%，擴大至$42億、相當於GDP的0.5%。商品貿易赤字由$689億增至$861億，國際收支也由$45億盈餘轉為$81億赤字。私人移轉收入由修正後的$332億增至$429億，緩衝了部分惡化。

印度央行提供優惠定價的美元兌盧比交換窗口，藉由鼓勵外幣存款與離岸債券融資，為外部收支壓力提供緩衝。6月至8月間，印度銀行透過該計畫發行$121.5億美元債券，其中超過75%來自民營銀行。Capri Global也計畫透過這項管道首次發行外幣債券，擬進行一筆3年3個月期的優先擔保交易，目標規模為$3億至$5億，初步殖利率指引約7.75%。這家非銀行貸款機構先前曾暫緩發行，因評級較高的銀行大量供給，使其所能取得的定價缺乏吸引力。

IMF的整體評估把這些個別案例連結到共同限制。全球公共債務接近GDP的100%，高於第二次世界大戰後的峰值；IMF並警告，財政壓力與停滯的反通膨進程正推升核心主權債殖利率。新興市場與低所得經濟體的融資條件改善並不均衡，而先進經濟體殖利率上升則增加外溢風險。沙烏地阿拉伯的超額認購與塞內加爾因重整而出現的債券損失形成強烈對比，顯示風險結果高度取決於信用品質、市場准入及既有債權人的待遇。

## 風險溢酬擴大之下，信用分歧進一步加深

美國信用債與美債同步轉弱，但單日走勢並不一致。投資級債利差小幅擴大，高收益債利差擴幅較明顯，硬通貨新興市場債利差也小幅走闊。主要上市債券基金經配息調整後的報酬全面為負：投資級債部位下跌0.93%，主要高收益債基金下跌約0.89%，新興市場債下跌0.72%。

儘管個別發行人與產業表現分歧，整體利差仍處於歷史偏窄水準。約$1兆、距到期超過三年的非金融投資級債，其交易利差相對各自評級異常寬，規模已超過年初的兩倍；其中美國約$5,800億，歐洲接近$4,000億。

這種錯位與美歐高評級債平均利差仍極窄的情況同時存在。美國平均利差僅0.78個百分點，歐洲為0.79個百分點，兩者都接近多年來的極端水準。六大超大規模雲端業者目前約占美國投資級債指數的5%，是兩年前的兩倍。其權重增長迫使追蹤指數的經理人重新平衡部位，即使整體利差幾乎不動，也可能推寬其他發行人的利差。

AI融資仍是這項技術性變化的核心。JPMorgan Asset Management策略師Stephanie Aliaga估計，由於最大型超大規模雲端業者的槓桿率仍低於整體市場，它們可輕鬆再增加$1.5兆債務。她預估2030年前AI基礎設施總支出將達$5.5兆，並指出營運現金流只能負擔部分所需支出，因此債務與替代資本勢不可少。

市場有能力吸收供給，並不代表所有相關證券風險相同。估計最大型科技公司今年近$2,000億的借款，約相當於私人投資人承接的美國中長期公債淨發行量25%。這種資金競爭會抬高兩個市場順利消化供給所需的殖利率，指數集中度也會改變不同企業發行人的相對利差。結果是市場整體仍可維持開放，但對個別發行人的選擇性大幅提高。

中升集團顯示正式信用評級與實際交易風險可以不同。儘管這家中國Mercedes-Benz經銷商仍維持投資級評級，其2028年到期美元債自7月以來殖利率一直高於10%。中國豪華車市場轉弱、電動車競爭加劇，使公司上半年獲利下跌89%、營收下降18.5%，新車銷售量減少17.6%。

截至6月底，中升持有人民幣136億元現金，足以償付明年到期的$3.5億聯貸與人民幣10億元債券。公司也已買回約$1.179億的2028年票據，使未償金額降至約$4.82億。這些資源提供再融資緩衝，但S&P已將發行人評級降至距非投資級僅一級；若需求與利潤率持續疲弱，仍有遭降為非投資級的風險。

HDFC Bank執行長Sashidhar Jagdishan意外決定不尋求續任後，其美元債連續第5個交易日走弱。2031年6月到期債券跌至面額每100美元報98.504美元，為發行以來最低；前一週出售的兩檔債券也跌至歷史低點。Moody’s表示，這項突如其來的接班安排帶來過渡風險，但銀行的基本信用狀況仍未受損。此一走勢顯示，即使沒有證據顯示資產負債表立即受損，公司治理不確定性仍會反映在債券價格上。

Brightspeed面對的負債問題更為急迫。這家由Apollo支持的寬頻業者在評估包括資產證券化在內的融資選項時，新增對其持續經營能力存在重大疑慮的警示。第二季營收下跌8.7%至$3.86億；上半年淨損$8.79億，營運現金流為負$3.41億，而截至6月30日持有現金$11.7億。

Brightspeed在2024年完成一筆被Moody’s歸類為困境債務交換的交易後，正為橫跨20州、資本需求龐大的光纖建設籌資。先前交易減少$11億債務並引進$37億新資本，但公司此後仍需額外資金。光纖服務銷售成長16%，網路涵蓋的可服務地點已超過300萬處；然而，持續經營警示顯示，營運進展尚未解決公司的槓桿與流動性負擔。

中國住房融資改革則處理另一種信用風險。新規定要求把購屋款存入託管帳戶；若建商未能按期交屋，買方可解除合約並取回款項；工程通常也必須封頂後才能預售。這套制度直接限制建商利用家庭預付款購地及為新建案融資的能力。

改革推出時，槓桿最高的民營建商多已倒閉，成屋交易量也已超過新屋。但截至2025年底，預售仍約占新屋購買量的75%，現有建案也將繼續適用舊制。Gavekal Dragonomics預期，受舊制保障的建案消化完畢後，2027年新開工量將明顯下滑。加強買方保障可降低完工風險，轉型期間卻可能進一步壓縮建商流動性與地方政府土地出售收入。

這些案例說明，信用指數表面平靜不能解讀為所有發行人都能同樣取得資金。沙烏地阿拉伯發債時，最終利差較初步指引收窄；超大規模雲端業者仍可考慮龐大發行，高評級債整體利差也依然狹窄。但塞內加爾的重整路徑、Brightspeed的融資需求、中升的交易殖利率及HDFC的領導層風險溢酬，同時顯示投資人正明確區分主權承受能力、營運現金流、擔保品與公司治理。

## 後續市場意義

美國下一輪政策考驗自9月3日開始。紐約時間上午8時30分公布的7月貿易赤字，預計由$733億擴大至$900億，將更新外部部門對第三季成長的貢獻。上午10時公布的ISM服務業指數，預計由54.1升至54.3；其中活動、就業與價格分項將顯示，製造業動能轉弱但成本偏高的組合，是否也延伸至規模更大的服務業。

8月非農就業報告將於9月4日上午8時30分公布。市場共識為新增58,000人，前值為減少23,000人；失業率預計維持4.1%。如果新增就業疲弱而失業率穩定，政策訊號將不同於勞動資源使用全面惡化。薪資成長與數據修正同樣重要，因為Barr是否願意繼續等待，取決於官員能否確信通膨正在降溫；Warsh則已將就業情勢描述為大致穩定。

9月11日公布的消費者物價報告，是聯準會9月15日至16日開會前最後一項主要通膨考驗。期貨目前反映升息機率約為三分之二。若廣泛價格壓力延續，升息理由將增強；若基礎通膨轉弱，即使油價仍高，Barr及其他官員也更有理由保持耐心。

勞動節造成交易中斷前後，美債供給的重要性將上升。財政部會在9月3日公布9月3年期、10年期與30年期公債的發行規模。美國固定收益市場9月7日休市，9月8日下午1時標售3年期公債，9月9日下午1時重開10年期公債；擴大長天期公債買回也預定9月9日開始。標售需求將顯示，在企業債供給龐大及官方買進並存之下，較高殖利率是否足以吸引私人資金承接。

日本本週四的30年期公債標售，是眼前全球長天期債券需求的重要考驗。10年期殖利率觸及3%後，該期公債標售取得3.29倍投標倍數；但超長期區段對各省廳創紀錄的預算申請、償債成本上升與增發風險更敏感。若標售順利，將顯示正殖利率回歸後，負債驅動型投資需求正延伸至曲線更長端；若結果疲弱，市場將重新質疑日本財政計畫需要多大的殖利率讓利。

ECB的9月10日決策已有明確訊號，市場完全反映升息25個基點至2.50%。政策指引將決定市場是否應保留未來一年再升息兩次的預期。關鍵在於，即使核心通膨已降至2.4%、服務通膨降至3.0%，能源推動的總體通膨壓力是否會由目前3.3%的水準進一步向外擴散。

BOJ將於9月17日至18日開會，市場對9月升息的定價已接近確定，日圓在創紀錄干預後仍然疲弱。因此，決策若要實質改變匯率及債券前景，不能只是確認市場廣泛預期的升息。投資人將尋找後續正常化速度的線索；政府完成預算時，也必須在各省廳約¥143兆申請與高市早苗把新增借款控制在¥40兆以下的目標間取得平衡。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries extended their selloff on Sept. 1 as renewed US-Iran fighting drove oil sharply higher, increased inflation compensation and strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise rates this month. The 2-year yield rose 5.8 basis points to 4.401%, the 5-year gained 5.5 basis points to 4.556%, the 10-year climbed 4.8 basis points to 4.799% and the 30-year added 3.2 basis points to 5.275%.

The concentration of the move from the front end through the 10-year sector produced a modest bear flattening. The 2s10s spread narrowed 1 basis point to 39.8 basis points, while 2s30s compressed 2.6 basis points to 87.4. Over the past week, the respective curves have flattened 5.7 and 11.7 basis points as investors marked up the prospective policy path more rapidly than long-term yields.

Inflation compensation supplied most of the latest nominal 10-year move. The 10-year breakeven increased 3.7 basis points to 2.358%, while the 10-year real yield rose 1.1 basis points to 2.441%. That differed from the previous session, when higher real yields had accounted for nearly all the increase. The change followed a 5.83% surge in WTI to $90.76 and a 5.23% rise in Brent to $95.22 after the US launched fresh strikes against Iran, Tehran retaliated and two oil tankers attempting to leave the Strait of Hormuz were struck by projectiles.

The energy shock landed in a market already primed for tighter policy by Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole message. Interest-rate futures put the probability of at least a quarter-point increase at the Sept. 15-16 meeting at 66.2%, up from 39.6% a week earlier. Fed Governor Michael Barr added a new conditional signal from the center of the committee: officials could remain patient if incoming data showed inflation moving toward 2%, but should act decisively if moderation proved insufficient.

US manufacturing offered no clean resolution. The Institute for Supply Management index fell to 54.6 in August from 55.6, below the 55.2 consensus, while new orders weakened. The prices-paid index nevertheless remained elevated at 71.1, and supplier deliveries slowed further. Job openings separately edged up in July, leaving labor demand subdued but stable rather than collapsing. The combination gave the Fed evidence of softer industrial momentum without the easing in costs that would clearly support another hold.

The rise in yields spread through risk assets without producing generalized market disorder. The S&P 500 fell 0.71%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 1.29% and the semiconductor index declined 2.14%. The Dollar Index rose 0.24%, while gold futures fell 1.21%. The VIX increased to 16.34, still well below levels associated with acute stress. US investment-grade spreads widened modestly, high-yield spreads widened more clearly and hard-currency emerging-market spreads moved modestly wider.

The defining feature of the session was therefore not a flight from risk into government bonds, but a global reassessment of the price of duration. Oil raised the near-term inflation hurdle, central-bank expectations shifted upward and fiscal and corporate supply continued to compete for capital. Japan’s 10-year yield reached 3% before an auction attracted acceptable demand, UK long yields climbed to levels last seen in 1998, and euro-area inflation strengthened the case for an ECB increase. Funding markets remained open—Saudi Arabia drew more than $15 billion of orders for a $3.25 billion sukuk—but the resilience of issuance did not prevent weaker sovereign and corporate credits from repricing sharply.

## Oil, Manufacturing and Barr Keep a September Fed Increase in Play

The latest oil move reflected a renewed physical threat around the Strait of Hormuz rather than a change in rhetoric alone. The US carried out strikes against Iranian targets after accusing Tehran of attempting to place mines in the strait and of attacking a US military base in Jordan. Iran said it retaliated, and projectiles hit two supertankers off Oman. The exchange followed several weeks of relative calm during which Washington had emphasized economic pressure and neither side had shown much willingness to restart negotiations after the collapse of an interim peace agreement.

WTI’s close above $90 and Brent’s move above $95 restored a direct energy channel to the inflation debate. The 10-year breakeven’s 3.7-basis-point rise showed that investors treated the shock as more than a transient geopolitical headline, though the level of 2.358% did not imply an unanchored long-term outlook. The simultaneous increase in real yields indicated that investors also required greater inflation-adjusted compensation as policy, supply and fiscal uncertainty remained elevated.

The shift in Fed expectations was substantial but still short of certainty. Futures assigned roughly a two-thirds probability to a September increase from the existing 3.50%-to-3.75% target range. That represented a marked change from the 39.6% probability recorded one week earlier, but preserved a meaningful chance that the committee would wait. The distinction matters because the market is assessing whether officials will respond to the first-round energy shock itself or to evidence that it is spreading into broader prices and expectations.

Barr’s remarks made that conditionality explicit. The Fed governor said officials could take more time if the data produced confidence that inflation was moderating toward 2%. If it was not moderating sufficiently, he said, the central bank should raise rates decisively. His intervention was notable because Reuters characterized him as a relatively centrist policymaker, while the July meeting had already produced three dissents in favor of an increase from Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari, Cleveland President Beth Hammack and Dallas President Lorie Logan.

The upcoming inflation reports remain central to Barr’s test, but the latest activity data did not provide the benign combination of weaker demand and lower costs that would make patience easy. The ISM manufacturing PMI declined 1 point to 54.6, remaining in expansion but missing both the 55.2 median forecast and the separate 55.0 forecast. New orders fell more sharply, to 53.7 from 56.7, indicating slower demand within the sector.

Cost and supply indicators moved differently. Prices paid held at 71.1, while supplier deliveries increased to 59.3 from 58.9, a higher reading that is consistent with slower deliveries. Survey respondents reported price increases across aluminum, steel, copper, electrical goods, fuel, memory products and semiconductors, along with shortages in several metals and electronics categories. ISM’s Susan Spence said 58% of respondent comments were negative, with companies citing price volatility, longer lead times, the Iran conflict and tariffs.

Other current indicators showed moderation rather than contraction. The Logistics Managers Index fell to 66.6 in August from 68.9 but remained expansionary. Redbook same-store sales growth accelerated to 9.6% in the week through Aug. 29 from 9.1%, retaining a firm nominal signal from household spending. July job openings increased to 7.27 million from 7.18 million, just below the 7.31 million median estimate, while terminations declined. None of those readings overrode the softer ISM headline, but together they offered little evidence of an abrupt demand break.

That mix explains why the front end could sell off even as manufacturing lost momentum. A weaker output measure normally reduces the need for restraint, but the prices component and the breadth of reported input pressures preserved the inflation risk. The market’s reaction function is increasingly sensitive not only to aggregate growth, but to whether energy, tariffs and AI-related demand for equipment and power are preventing cost pressure from cooling.

The long end faced a separate hurdle. The 30-year yield returned to 5.275%, approximately where it stood immediately before Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced expanded buybacks on Aug. 19. Those purchases are not scheduled to begin until Sept. 9, and Treasury has said only that operations in 10- to 30-year securities will at least double. The announcement temporarily improved the tone, but it did not remove the underlying government financing requirement or the competition from corporate borrowers.

September investment-grade corporate issuance is expected to reach about $215 billion after record August supply, much of it associated with the artificial-intelligence buildout. The 30-year yield has already settled above 5% on 55 days this year, the most in any year since 2006, and it came into September after rising about 65 basis points from its 2026 low. Options traders have paid for protection against another increase, including a $6.5 million position targeting a 30-year yield as high as 5.7% by late November.

The latest curve move did not resemble an uncontrolled long-end rupture. Shorter benchmark yields rose more than the 30-year rate, and Treasury-market volatility remained contained. Cash activity also declined from the unusually heavy previous session: FINRA recorded $1.262 trillion of Treasury par traded, 30.6% less than on Aug. 31, including $1.037 trillion of nominal coupons. The decline in turnover does not establish investor direction, but it shows that the yield adjustment occurred without another surge in transaction volume.

## Japan’s 3% Yield Finds Demand as Policy and Fiscal Pressure Intensify

Japan’s 10-year government-bond yield reached 3% for the first time since 1996 and later traded at 3.005%, completing a rapid repricing from roughly half that level a year earlier. The move extended across the curve: the 2-year yield reached 1.81%, its highest in 31 years, the 5-year touched a record 2.265%, the 20-year climbed to 3.885% and the 30-year was positioned near a record closing level around 4.18%.

The immediate 10-year auction showed that higher yields were beginning to attract demand. Its bid-to-cover ratio rose to 3.29 from 2.56 at the previous sale and was slightly above the 12-month average of 3.26. The tail narrowed, and MUFJ Morgan Stanley took down 22% of the offering. The result allowed the 10-year yield to ease modestly after reaching the milestone, contrasting with the weak 2-year auction held the previous week.

Demand was solid rather than unequivocally strong. SMBC Nikko strategist Miki Den said investors appeared to require a yield above 3%, while the average auction yield was close enough to that threshold to recruit buyers. The 30-year auction due Thursday presents a more difficult test because super-long securities carry greater exposure to fiscal expansion, additional issuance and the long-run normalization of Japanese rates.

The policy repricing has become nearly complete for September. Overnight-index swaps implied a roughly 99% probability of action at the BOJ’s Sept. 17-18 meeting in the latest Bloomberg account, compared with less than half that probability a month earlier. The central bank last increased its policy rate in June to 1%, the highest in 31 years. Higher short and intermediate yields now reflect expectations that the BOJ will respond again to inflation and persistent yen weakness.

Bessent strengthened that expectation after meeting BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda during the Group of 20 gathering in North Carolina. The US Treasury said Bessent strongly supported decisive Japanese market and monetary steps to address substantial yen undervaluation, noted that currency weakness was contributing to domestic inflation and emphasized policy communication that anchors expectations and avoids excessive exchange-rate volatility.

His intervention exposed a disagreement over how directly Washington had discussed Japanese monetary policy. Treasury Under Secretary Erin Browne said Bessent told Ueda and Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama that Japan’s next step should be a rate increase. Katayama denied discussing the specific conduct of monetary policy with him and emphasized the BOJ’s legal independence. She did say both sides agreed that orderly yen movements were important for global financial stability and that coordinated efforts had been beneficial.

The distinction did little to reduce the market pressure. The yen breached 160 per dollar during Tokyo trading despite Japan’s record ¥15.4 trillion of intervention over the preceding month and US participation in the July 31 operation. Bessent has increasingly presented BOJ tightening as preferable to repeated currency intervention, and the Treasury’s formal readout aligned US concerns about the yen with Japan’s domestic inflation problem.

Fiscal policy is reinforcing the upward pressure on JGB yields. Japanese ministries requested roughly ¥143 trillion for fiscal 2027, the highest total on record and above the approximately ¥140.6 trillion combined size of the current initial budget and the previous year’s supplementary budgets. The Economy Ministry sought more than five times its prior-year amount, while defense and welfare requests also set records.

Part of the increase reflects Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s attempt to move spending traditionally added through supplementary budgets into the initial plan and to create a multi-year framework for growth investment. That improves transparency, but it does not eliminate the financing requirement. Some spending amounts remain open and could rise during the budget process, while the Finance Ministry is already seeking a record ¥36.6 trillion for debt service.

Takaichi has said she wants to keep new bond issuance below ¥40 trillion. Achieving that goal will depend on how aggressively the government pares ministry requests and whether revenue meets its assumptions. Japan’s gross public debt remains above 200% of GDP, and the government used a 3% long-term interest-rate assumption when estimating fiscal 2026 debt-service costs. The market has now reached that rate in the benchmark 10-year maturity.

Higher yields create a countervailing demand channel. The 10-year has moved above funding costs for banks and liability costs for life insurers, and domestic bonds are becoming more competitive with overseas securities for Japanese institutions. International investors, meanwhile, account for about two-thirds of monthly cash JGB transactions, up from 12% in 2009, increasing the market’s sensitivity to global positioning as well as domestic balance-sheet demand.

The auction demonstrated that 3% can attract capital without establishing a ceiling. The prospective BOJ increase, yen weakness and fiscal requests all point toward a higher-rate regime, while the yield itself improves the economics of domestic ownership. Thursday’s 30-year sale will show whether that demand extends to the part of the curve most exposed to future supply and debt-service risk.

## European Inflation and UK Rates Extend the Global Tightening Cycle

Euro-area inflation accelerated to 3.3% in August from 2.9% in July, the highest rate since September 2023 and in line with the median estimate. The result made a quarter-point increase in the European Central Bank’s deposit rate to 2.50% on Sept. 10 a near-certainty in market pricing. It would be the ECB’s second increase of 2026.

The internal composition was less uniformly hawkish than the headline. Core inflation eased to 2.4% from 2.5%, while services inflation slowed to 3.0% from 3.3%. Headline rates increased in Germany, France, Italy and Spain as elevated oil and gas prices fed through, but the decline in underlying measures showed that broad second-round effects had not yet become evident.

Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel called the fall in core and services inflation positive and said the next policy decision was relatively predictable, consistent with the fully priced September move. Lithuanian Governor Gediminas Simkus took a firmer view of the path beyond next week. He argued that a September increase would not be sufficient, citing higher natural-gas and agricultural prices and stronger-than-expected European growth as reasons for the projected rate path to move higher.

Those positions define the next debate more clearly than the September decision itself. The current 2.25% deposit rate is below the 2.5% level ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane has described as the upper end of the neutral range. A quarter-point increase would reach that boundary. Market pricing implied two additional increases over the following year, while economists and some policymakers saw a high probability that the ECB could stop after September. December, when officials receive another set of staff projections, is a likely point for reassessment.

The global selloff was especially severe in the UK as gilts caught up after a holiday. The 10-year yield rose as much as 11 basis points to 5.25%, while the 30-year reached 5.89%, its highest since May 1998. Markets priced two Bank of England increases by February, reflecting both the energy shock and concern that the UK’s limited fiscal room could leave long maturities unusually exposed.

Bank of England policymaker Catherine Mann reinforced the domestic case for restraint. She said economic growth had strengthened since the previous meeting, the labor market appeared to be stabilizing and inflation was somewhat higher than expected. Mann had voted for a 25-basis-point increase at the previous meeting and argued that rates set modestly too high could later be corrected, indicating that she assigns greater cost to allowing inflation risk to persist.

Markets fully priced a BOE increase by year-end but assigned only about a 15% probability to action in September. Current housing and credit data explain some of that caution. Mortgage approvals fell to 56,053 in July from 58,215, below the 59,400 expectation and the lowest since January 2024. Approvals have remained below 60,000 for three consecutive months as the average 2-year fixed mortgage rate rose to 5.59% from 4.83% before the Iran conflict.

House prices offered a mixed signal. Nationwide reported a 0.2% increase in August to an average £275,465, slightly above the 0.1% forecast and reversing a downwardly revised 0.1% decline in July. Prices were 1.6% higher than a year earlier, but they had fallen in three preceding monthly readings and remained constrained by higher financing costs. Unsecured consumer borrowing increased by £2 billion in July from £1.9 billion, while household bank deposits slowed to £3.8 billion from £6.2 billion, suggesting consumers were using borrowing and savings to cushion pressure on real incomes.

Israel moved in the opposite policy direction. The Bank of Israel cut its rate by 25 basis points to 3.25%, its third consecutive reduction after moves in May and July. The decision had been finely balanced: nine of 18 surveyed economists expected a cut and nine expected no change. The shekel weakened to 3.02 per dollar afterward but remained near historically strong levels, which had prompted exporters to seek additional monetary relief.

The central bank cited moderating inflation and said activity looked softer once production abroad by Israeli companies was excluded, despite annualized second-quarter GDP growth of 15.4% following an earlier war-related contraction. Guidance remained conditional on inflation, activity, geopolitics and fiscal developments. Israel’s easing therefore reflected its domestic inflation and currency position rather than a broader decline in global price pressure; the widening contrast with other developed-market policy paths may itself become a constraint if it places sustained pressure on the shekel.

## Sovereign Funding Remains Open but Credit Outcomes Diverge

The global duration selloff spread into emerging markets as higher US rate expectations and oil prices weakened demand for riskier debt. Credit-default swaps on a group of 30 developing-country sovereigns rose for a fourth day. JPMorgan data showed the spread on EM dollar bonds had already widened 6 basis points to 235 on Monday, while local-currency bonds extended their decline from the record reached on Aug. 25.

The broad move did not close primary markets. Saudi Arabia sold $3.25 billion of 5- and 10-year sukuk, drawing orders that peaked above $15 billion. The 10-year tranche priced 80 basis points over Treasuries, about 30 basis points tighter than initial discussions. Proceeds will support general budget purposes, and the successful execution showed that a highly active sovereign borrower could still compress pricing despite direct economic exposure to the Hormuz conflict.

Saudi funding needs remain substantial. The economy suffered its deepest quarterly contraction since the pandemic in Q2 as oil activity weakened, and the government is also in early discussions over a loan of at least $8 billion. Before Tuesday’s deal, the sovereign had raised about $6 billion in domestic and international bonds this year, while Saudi Aramco and the Public Investment Fund had issued another $11 billion between them. Healthy demand reduced the immediate placement risk without removing the fiscal consequences of lower production and regional conflict.

Senegal experienced the opposite market response after making its prospective debt treatment explicit. Its euro-denominated bonds due in 2028 fell 6.9 cents to 49.44 cents, while the sovereign spread rose to 1,745 basis points from 1,651. The government said it would proceed under an improved version of the Group of 20 Common Framework after reaching a staff-level agreement on a new $2.2 billion IMF program.

The IMF agreement is preliminary and requires executive-board approval. It depends on corrective measures addressing previously undisclosed debt, the discovery of which caused the fund to suspend an earlier $1.8 billion facility. Finance Minister Cheikh Diba said the government preferred a tailored and less disruptive restructuring approach, but promised an implementation schedule and further details in the coming weeks.

The price decline showed that investors interpreted the announcement as increasing the likelihood of concessions. Senegal requires about 6 trillion CFA francs, or $10.6 billion, of annual financing and plans to raise roughly 4 trillion CFA francs in the regional market this year. Structured funding, including total-return swaps, has helped bridge the loss of international access but has also come under IMF scrutiny. The new program could eventually lower financing costs; it does not settle the maturity treatment, recovery value or timetable.

South Korea added another large sovereign-supply plan. The government proposed issuing 222.8 trillion won of bonds in 2027, close to this year’s record 232 trillion won plan. Of the proposed total, 110.7 trillion won would refinance maturing debt and 15.9 trillion would support market-making operations, leaving net issuance of about 96.3 trillion won.

The borrowing will help finance a 12.8% increase in spending to a record 820.9 trillion won under President Lee Jae Myung’s expansionary agenda. Korea’s 3-year yield rose 6 basis points to 3.9% and the 10-year gained 9 basis points to 4.4%. The issuance proposal still requires parliamentary approval, and prior experience shows lawmakers can reduce the final amount, but a total above 200 trillion won disappointed investors who had expected buoyant semiconductor tax receipts to permit a sharper reduction.

Brazil’s economy supplied a different constraint on local rates. GDP grew 0.5% in Q2, slowing from 1.1% but exceeding the 0.4% median forecast. Output was 2.0% higher than a year earlier, also above the 1.8% expectation. Agriculture expanded 2.8%, services grew 0.2% and industry increased 0.1%, while household consumption contracted 0.4% for its first decline in three quarters.

The composition showed a widening division between resilient headline growth and rate-sensitive demand. Construction and manufacturing contracted, and fixed investment’s 1.2% increase was much slower than in Q1. With mid-August inflation at 4.24% against a 3% target and the Selic rate at 14%, the central bank has limited room to accelerate the easing cycle even as officials expect another slowdown in Q3.

India’s external accounts also became more dependent on financing flows. The current-account deficit widened to $4.2 billion, or 0.5% of GDP, in the April-June quarter from a revised $3.4 billion, or 0.4%, a year earlier. The merchandise deficit increased to $86.1 billion from $68.9 billion, and the balance of payments shifted to an $8.1 billion deficit from a $4.5 billion surplus. Private transfers improved to $42.9 billion from a revised $33.2 billion, cushioning part of the deterioration.

The Reserve Bank of India’s discounted dollar-rupee swap window provides an offset by encouraging foreign-currency deposits and offshore bond funding. Indian banks raised $12.15 billion in dollar bonds from June through August under the program, more than 75% from private lenders. Capri Global entered that channel with plans for its first foreign-currency bond, a three-year-and-three-month senior secured transaction targeting $300 million to $500 million with initial guidance near 7.75%. The non-bank lender had postponed an earlier attempt when heavy, higher-rated bank issuance made pricing unattractive.

The IMF’s broader assessment connected these individual cases to a common constraint. It put worldwide public debt near 100% of GDP, above post-World War II peaks, and warned that fiscal pressure and stalled disinflation were lifting core sovereign yields. Financing conditions for emerging and low-income economies have improved unevenly, but the rise in advanced-economy yields increases spillover risk. The divergence between Saudi Arabia’s oversubscribed deal and Senegal’s restructuring-driven losses showed how sharply that risk depends on credit quality, market access and the treatment of existing creditors.

## Credit Dispersion Deepens Beneath Wider Risk Premiums

US credit weakened alongside Treasuries, but the daily move was not uniform. Investment-grade spreads widened modestly, high-yield spreads widened more clearly and hard-currency EM spreads widened modestly. Distribution-adjusted returns were negative across the principal listed bond funds: investment-grade exposure lost 0.93%, the main high-yield funds fell about 0.89%, and emerging-market debt declined 0.72%.

Broad spread levels remained historically tight even as individual issuers and sectors diverged. Approximately $1 trillion of nonfinancial investment-grade bonds with more than three years to maturity were trading at spreads unusually wide for their ratings, more than double the amount at the start of the year. About $580 billion was in the US and almost $400 billion in Europe.

That dislocation coexisted with average high-grade spreads of only 0.78 percentage point in the US and 0.79 percentage point in Europe, both near multiyear extremes. The six largest hyperscalers now account for about 5% of the US investment-grade index, twice their share two years ago. Their growth forces index-aware managers to rebalance and can widen other issuers even when aggregate spreads barely move.

AI financing remains central to that technical shift. JPMorgan Asset Management strategist Stephanie Aliaga estimated that the largest hyperscalers could comfortably add another $1.5 trillion of debt because their leverage remains below that of the broader market. She projected total AI infrastructure expenditure of $5.5 trillion by 2030 and argued that debt and alternative capital will be necessary because operating cash flow will cover only part of the required spending.

The capacity to absorb supply does not make all related securities equivalent. Nearly $200 billion borrowed by the largest technology firms this year was estimated to equal about 25% of net Treasury note and bond issuance to private investors. That competition raises the yield needed to clear both markets, while index concentration changes relative spreads among corporate issuers. The result is a market that can remain open at the headline level while becoming much more selective underneath.

Zhongsheng Group illustrated the distinction between formal rating and traded risk. The Chinese Mercedes-Benz dealer’s 2028 dollar bond has yielded more than 10% since July despite the company retaining an investment-grade rating. First-half profit fell 89%, revenue declined 18.5% and new-vehicle sales volumes dropped 17.6% as China’s luxury-car market weakened and electric-vehicle competition intensified.

The company held 13.6 billion yuan of cash at the end of June, enough to cover a $350 million syndicated loan and a 1 billion yuan bond due next year. It also repurchased about $117.9 million of its 2028 notes, leaving approximately $482 million outstanding. Those resources provide a refinancing cushion, but S&P has already lowered the issuer to one notch above junk, leaving fallen-angel risk if weak demand and margins persist.

HDFC Bank’s dollar bonds weakened for a fifth session after Chief Executive Officer Sashidhar Jagdishan unexpectedly decided not to seek reappointment. Its June 2031 note fell to 98.504 cents, the lowest since issuance, while two bonds sold the previous week also reached record lows. Moody’s said the unanticipated succession introduced transition risk, though the bank’s underlying creditworthiness remained intact. The move showed governance uncertainty reaching bond prices even without evidence of immediate balance-sheet impairment.

Brightspeed presented a more acute liability problem. The Apollo-backed broadband provider added a substantial doubt warning about its ability to continue as a going concern as it explored financing options, including an asset-backed securitization. Q2 revenue fell 8.7% to $386 million. For the first half, it recorded an $879 million net loss and $341 million of negative operating cash flow, against $1.17 billion of cash at June 30.

The company is funding a capital-intensive fiber build across 20 states after completing a transaction in 2024 that Moody’s classified as a distressed exchange. That earlier deal cut debt by $1.1 billion and brought in $3.7 billion of new capital, but Brightspeed has required additional funding since then. Fiber sales rose 16% and the network passed 3 million enabled locations, yet the going-concern language showed that operational progress had not resolved its leverage and liquidity burden.

China’s housing-finance reform addressed a different source of credit risk. New rules require homebuyers’ payments to be placed in escrow, allow buyers to terminate contracts and receive refunds if developers miss delivery dates, and generally prevent pre-sales until construction has topped out. The regime directly limits developers’ ability to fund land purchases and new projects with advance payments from households.

The reform arrives after the most leveraged private developers have already failed and existing-home transactions have overtaken new-home sales. Pre-sales nevertheless accounted for about 75% of new-home purchases at the end of 2025, and current projects will remain under the old rules. Gavekal Dragonomics expects a sizable drop in new starts in 2027 when that grandfathered pipeline runs down. Stronger buyer protection can reduce completion risk, but the transition may further constrain developer liquidity and land-sale revenue for local governments.

These cases explain why calm index-level credit cannot be read as uniform access to capital. Saudi Arabia tightened pricing through initial guidance, hyperscalers can still contemplate enormous issuance and broad high-grade spreads remain narrow. At the same time, Senegal’s restructuring path, Brightspeed’s financing need, Zhongsheng’s traded yield and HDFC’s leadership premium show that investors are distinguishing sharply among sovereign capacity, operating cash flow, collateral and governance.

## Forward Market Significance

The next US policy tests begin Sept. 3. The July trade deficit is expected to widen to $90 billion from $73.3 billion at 8:30 a.m. New York time, updating the external contribution to Q3 growth. At 10 a.m., the ISM services index is expected at 54.3 after 54.1. Its activity, employment and prices readings will show whether manufacturing’s combination of slower momentum and elevated costs extends into the much larger services economy.

August payrolls follow Sept. 4 at 8:30 a.m. Consensus calls for a 58,000 increase after a 23,000 decline, with unemployment unchanged at 4.1%. A weak payroll headline accompanied by stable unemployment would present a different policy signal from a broad deterioration in labor utilization. Wage growth and revisions will also matter because Barr’s conditional willingness to wait depends on confidence that inflation is moderating, while Warsh has described employment as broadly steady.

The Sept. 11 consumer-price report is the final major inflation test before the Fed meets Sept. 15-16. Futures currently assign roughly a two-thirds probability to an increase. A continuation of broad price pressure would strengthen the case for action; softer underlying inflation would give Barr and other officials grounds to extend patience even if oil remains elevated.

Treasury supply becomes more prominent around the Labor Day interruption. The department will announce sizes for the September 3-year, 10-year and 30-year sales on Sept. 3. The US fixed-income market is closed Sept. 7, followed by the 3-year auction at 1 p.m. on Sept. 8 and the 10-year reopening at 1 p.m. on Sept. 9. Expanded long-maturity buybacks are also due to begin Sept. 9. Auction demand will show whether higher yields are attracting sufficient private sponsorship alongside heavy corporate issuance and official purchases.

Japan’s 30-year auction on Thursday is the immediate global-duration test. The 10-year sale achieved a 3.29 bid-to-cover ratio after the yield reached 3%, but the super-long sector carries greater sensitivity to record ministry budget requests, rising debt-service costs and the risk of additional issuance. A smooth result would show that the return of positive yields is recruiting liability-driven demand farther out the curve; a weak one would reopen the question of how much concession Japan’s fiscal program requires.

The ECB’s Sept. 10 decision is heavily signaled, with a 25-basis-point increase to 2.50% fully priced. Guidance will determine whether markets should retain expectations for two more increases over the following year. The key distinction is whether energy-driven headline inflation begins to spread beyond the current 3.3% rate even as core inflation has eased to 2.4% and services to 3.0%.

The BOJ meets Sept. 17-18 with a September increase priced close to certainty and the yen still weak despite record intervention. The decision must therefore do more than confirm a widely expected move to change the currency and bond outlook materially. Investors will look for evidence on the pace of later normalization, while the government’s final budget work must reconcile roughly ¥143 trillion of ministry requests with Takaichi’s objective of keeping new borrowing below ¥40 trillion.

Credit outcomes will depend on transaction terms and execution. Senegal must disclose the timetable and creditor treatment under its proposed Common Framework process, while the IMF executive board still has to approve the $2.2 billion program. Brightspeed must obtain financing sufficient to address its going-concern warning, and China’s developers and local governments must absorb the transition from advance-payment funding to escrow-backed sales. Across those cases, continued market access will matter less than the priority, maturity, collateral and cash-flow protection attached to the new money.

Heavy AI-related borrowing is reshaping investment-grade indices and competing with Treasury supply, while Zhongsheng’s fallen-angel risk, HDFC Bank’s succession uncertainty and Brightspeed’s going-concern warning showed investors differentiating among operating cash flow, liquidity and governance. US services, payrolls and Sept. 11 CPI will determine whether slower manufacturing and elevated costs extend across the economy before the Sept. 15-16 Fed meeting. Treasury and Japanese auctions will test demand for duration amid heavy public and corporate supply, while ECB and BOJ guidance must clarify whether expected September moves begin longer tightening paths. Credit outcomes will turn on financing and restructuring terms, not access alone.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries sell off as oil shock lifts inflation compensation and September Fed odds
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries extended their selloff after renewed US-Iran fighting disrupted tankers near the Strait of Hormuz and drove WTI up 5.83% to $90.76 and Brent up 5.23% to $95.22. The 2-year yield rose 5.8 basis points to 4.401%, the 5-year gained 5.5 basis points to 4.556%, the 10-year climbed 4.8 basis points to 4.799% and the 30-year added 3.2 basis points to 5.275%, producing a modest bear flattening.

Inflation compensation supplied most of the 10-year move: the breakeven rose 3.7 basis points to 2.358%, while the real yield increased 1.1 basis points to 2.441%. Futures lifted the probability of a Sept. 15-16 Fed increase to 66.2% from 39.6% a week earlier. Manufacturing slowed but remained expansionary, while elevated prices paid and slower supplier deliveries denied policymakers a clean combination of weaker demand and cooling costs.

The reassessment extended globally. Japan’s 10-year yield reached 3% before an auction attracted acceptable demand, euro-area inflation strengthened the case for a Sept. 10 ECB increase and UK long yields reached levels last seen in 1998. Primary funding remained open, illustrated by Saudi Arabia’s oversubscribed sukuk, but weaker sovereign and corporate credits repriced sharply as investors distinguished more aggressively among fiscal capacity, liquidity and governance.
